:::{#thm-adjoint-inner-product}
#### The adjoint property for inner products

Let $\matr{A}$ be an $m \times n$ complex matrix.
Under the standard inner product on complex Euclidean space, $\iprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}} \eqdef \vecf{u}^{\mathsf{H}}\vecf{v}$,

$$\iprod{\matr{A}\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}} = \iprod{\vecf{u}}{\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}}\vecf{v}}
\quad \text{for all } \vecf{u} \in \mathbb{C}^n \text{ and } \vecf{v} \in \mathbb{C}^m.$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

By the definition of the standard complex inner product and the product rule for the Hermitian adjoint (@thm-hermitian-adjoint-properties):

$$
\ba
\iprod{\matr{A}\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}
&= (\matr{A}\vecf{u})^{\mathsf{H}}\vecf{v}
&& \text{(definition of standard inner product)}
\\
&= (\vecf{u}^{\mathsf{H}}\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}})\vecf{v}
&& \text{(@thm-hermitian-adjoint-properties, reversal of products)}
\\
&= \vecf{u}^{\mathsf{H}}(\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}}\vecf{v})
&& \text{(associativity of matrix multiplication)}
\\
&= \iprod{\vecf{u}}{\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}}\vecf{v}}
&& \text{(definition of standard inner product)}.
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-adjoint-name}
#### Where the name "adjoint" comes from

This identity is the origin of the name **adjoint**:
in functional analysis and operator theory,
the *adjoint* of a linear map $T: V \to W$ between inner product spaces is defined as the unique operator $T^*: W \to V$ satisfying
$\iprod{T\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}} = \iprod{\vecf{u}}{T^*\vecf{v}}$ (@axler2024linear [Definition 7.1, p. 226]).
When $V$ and $W$ are finite-dimensional spaces equipped with their standard orthonormal bases,
the matrix representing the adjoint operator $T^*$ is precisely the Hermitian adjoint matrix $\matr{A}^{\mathsf{H}}$ (@axler2024linear [Proposition 7.9, p. 231]).

:::
